cohort: The study included 207 parturients who delivered via vagina, divided into a PPH group (n=102) and a non-PPH group (n=105).
finding: Fibrinogen, D-dimer, and neonatal weight are good predictors for postpartum hemorrhage in vaginal delivery, with fibrinogen being the best single predictor, and their combination offering a more comprehensive prediction.
mod_finding: N/A (The study exclusively focused on vaginal deliveries and did not compare or analyze different modes of birth or findings related to mode of birth variations.)
cross-section timing: Peripartum/Immediately postpartum (measurements taken around the time of delivery to predict PPH)
birth_weight: N/A (Neonatal weight was an exposure variable, not a selection criterion for a specific weight range)
